minutes.headline: Select Board reappointed the animal control officer after an open hearing; filled Board of Health and Planning Board seats.
minutes.summary: Joint appointments filled a Board of Health seat and a Planning Board vacancy, the latter by roll call with a remote member. The board held an open-session discussion of animal control procedure, heard residents support the officer, then moved to reappoint her. It also adopted personnel policies, heard about a SNAP outreach program at the Council on Aging, and discussed painting the Town Hall.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board vacancy was filled by a 5-4 roll call vote at a joint meeting, with one member taking part remotely.
The Select Board held an open discussion of animal control procedure, heard residents and the shelter support the officer, then moved to reappoint her; the vote was not audible.
A joint Board of Health appointment was nominated by voice vote; a citizen's floor nomination was ruled out because citizens cannot make motions at a joint meeting.
An 11-policy employee handbook package was approved, and the personnel policies were moved as amended; the town counsel access policy returns with office hours.
The Town Hall painting will go ahead, with color feedback sought at the next meeting; the Council on Aging was accepted for state SNAP outreach money.

why_it_matters: Planning Board seats shape zoning and development decisions, and this seat was settled by a single vote.
The new personnel policies set rules for town employees and are paid for through the town budget, mostly taxes.
The SNAP outreach money goes to the general fund and needs no extra budget this year, while the Town Hall mold abatement was supplemented by a reserve fund transfer.
watch_next: Next meeting: color feedback on the Town Hall painting, and the revised town counsel access policy with office hours.
